claims.claim: Arrival scene, the Record of the hearing (Relatio motionis), in the Latin of Migne PG 90: 'circa solis occasum, venientes, duo mandatores cum decem excubitoribus, tulerunt eos e navi nudos nudique pedes' ('tum scilicet domnus Maximus, tum socius ejus'). The Life has him led off 'nudis pedibus ... ac sine amiculo'. 'Without cloaks' renders 'nudos' with the Life's 'sine amiculo'
claims.witness: PG90 (maximus-confessor_relatio-motionis-disputatio-bizyae-grc-lat_migne-pg90.txt) l.6783-6790; Life l.4974-4977 [OCR forms: 'ſurore' later in the passage]

claims.claim: First hearing: 'post dies aliquot adducunt eos ad palatium, introque sistunt Senem, quo loco senatus aliaque multa turba convenerant'; 'ditit ei sacellarius cum multa ira ei ſurore, Christianus es? Et ait, Gratia Christi, universorum Dei, Christianus sum. Cui ille, Non est verum. Respondit Dei servus, Tu dicis; sed Deus scit esse me Christianum, et perseveranter esse.' The brief tells the exchange in modern words; 'the emperor's treasurer' renders 'sacellarius'
claims.witness: PG90 l.6791-6803 [OCR forms: 'ditit' for 'dixit', 'ei ſurore' for 'et furore']

claims.claim: The treason charge: 'Tu enim solus Egyptum et Alexandriam et Pentapolim et Tripolim et Africam Saracenis tradidisti.' The brief names three of the five places. Combefis's section head reads 'Majestatis crimen et depulsio'

The record's title: 'Relatio motionis facte inter domnum abbatem Maximum el socium ejus atque principes in secretario'. Fabricius's notice, printed in PG 90: parts are given 'Latine ex Anastasii bibliothecarii versione'
claims.witness: PG90 l.6728-6747; l.289-293 [OCR forms: 'el' for 'et', 'lan- tum' for 'tantum']

claims.claim: Date of the hearing, 655: Louis Duchesne, 'ses apocrisiaires arrivèrent à Constantinople peu de temps avant la Pentecôte, 17 mai 655 ... comme il résulte des dates fournies par les interrogatoires de saint Maxime'; the record has Maximus told 'heri venerunt apocrisiarii Romani, et cras Dominico die communicabunt patriarche'. The admonition in Mansi 11: 'Rem anno 655. superstite adhuc Martino'. Duchesne dates the envoys; the hearing's year follows from the record's 'yesterday'
claims.witness: DUCHESNE LP1 (liber-pontificalis_texte-introduction-commentaire-t1-lat-fra_duchesne1886.txt) l.163416-163421; PG90 l.7646-7651; MANSI11 (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-11-lat_welter-facsimile1901.txt) l.808-812 [OCR forms: 'Gonstantinople', 'fuperftice']

claims.claim: Greek Life (Vita ac Certamen, Combefis's Latin): born in Constantinople, 'patria quidem, primo exstitit urbium magnaque Constantinopolis'; 'Parentes, antiqua prosapia nobiles'; Heraclius 'eorum qui a seeretis imperatori essent, principem esse jubente'; left as 'Monothelitarum dogma consurgens' spread, for the monastery 'quod in adverso situm littore est, ac Chrysopolis dicitur'. Fabricius: 'ex protosecretario Heraclii imp., monachus'

The Life is a work in his honor: heading 'IN VITAM AC CERTAMEN SANCTI PATRIS NOSTRI AC CONFESSORIS MAXIMI'; it closes with the author's peroration to Maximus (section XLI, 'Auctoris ad Maximum peroratio', l.6603)

Typos: Martin's speech, as copied into the Book of the Popes' Life of Martin (Mansi 10): 'nec unam, nec duas voluntates, aut operationes in Christo domino nostro definiens confiteri'; William Dudley Foulke, in his notes to Paul the Deacon: 'Finally, Constans in 648 ... issued his Type, forbidding controversy upon both sides.' Duchesne: the Life's passage is 'emprunté mot à mot au discours du pape Martin'
claims.witness: MANSI10 (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-10-lat_welter-facsimile1901.txt) l.81990-81996; FOULKE (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt) l.9936-9939; DUCHESNE LP1 l.162719 [OCR forms: long s as 'f', 'fcilicer', 'noftro', 'con- troversy']

claims.claim: Debate with Pyrrhus in Africa: the Disputation's Latin heading has it held 'Gregorii patricii opera'; the editor's monitum, 'Fuisse habitam in Africa disputationem'; Fabricius dates it 645 ('cum Pyrrho, ex-patriarcha Constantinopol., disputationem habuisset a. 645'). In the record, Troilus and Sergius Eucrates ask about 'motionem dogmatum, quz facta est inter te et Pyrrhum in Africa et Rome: et quibus ei verbis persuaseris anathematizare proprium dogma'
claims.witness: PG91 (maximus-confessor_disputatio-cum-pyrrho-pg91-grc-lat_migne1860.txt) l.15117-15119, 15055-15060; PG90 l.279-281, 7499-7504 [OCR forms: 'Gregorit - pairicis', 'babuisset', 'Die nobis']

claims.claim: Why he would not take communion: 'Non communicas throno Constantinopolitano? Et dicit, Non communico.' ... 'quatuor concilia ejecerunt, per illa novem capitula, quæ facta sunt Alexandriæ; et per ecthesim, quæ in hac urbe Sergio auctore edita est; et per typum, qui nuper, id est, per sextam indictionem, promulgatus est' ... 'ipsique seipsos toties deposuerunt'. The brief names the Typos and 'an earlier statement by the patriarch Sergius' (the ecthesis issued 'Sergio auctore'); the card names all three

Two wills and workings: 'Num ergo prorsus necesse est ut voluntates et operationes in Christo dicantur? Respondit : Plane necesse, si vere pie sentire volumus.' ... 'Nam Patres palam dicant, neque esse neque cognosci ullam quoquomodo naturam, absque substantiali sua operatione.' Told in modern words
Own teaching: 'Ego dogma proprium non habeo, sed commune Ecclesiæ catholicæ.' Said to Troilus and Sergius Eucrates on the evening of the hearing. Told in modern words as the close

Theophanes the Confessor, in Migne's Latin: 'Tum vero Maximus ex Africa Romam transfretatus, Martini papæ sanctum in Deum ardorem accendit, qui centum et quinquaginta episcoporum synodo celebrata, Sergium et Pyrrhum, Cyrum et Paulum anathemate perculerunt.' Theophanes is 'ABBATIS AGRI ET CONFESSORIS' in PG 108
claims.witness: THEOPHANES (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863.txt) l.60747-60752, 138 [OCR forms: 'Matimus et Africa', 'ardorem-accendit', '8ynodo', 'Cyrum of Paulum', 'pervule- runt']

claims.claim: Synod of 649: Lateran, Martin I, condemning Sergius and Pyrrhus with Cyrus and Paul (Book of the Popes in Mansi 10; Bede IV.17-18; the Roman Breviary)

Bizya: 'sanctus quidem senex, Bizyæ, provinciæ Thraciæ castro, ejus autem discipulus Perberi'. Mansi 11: 'Disputatio Maximi cum Theodosio Cæsareæ in Bithynia episcopo'. Theodosius: 'Nos ... jubemus pro domino nostro imperatore, te communicante, sublatum iri Typum.' Maximus: 'Suscipiant horum damnationem, quæ Romæ per pia dogmata atque regulas synodice edita est'. Theodosius: 'Non habuit robur, quæ Romæ celebrata synodus est, ut quæ injussu imperatoris habita est.' Maximus: 'Si habitas synodos imperatorum jussiones firmant, non autem pia fides, etiam synodos contra homoousion habitas suscipiant'
claims.witness: PG90 l.8275-8278, 9566-9586; MANSI11 l.5565-5569 [OCR forms: 'provinciz', '(6) Typum', 'Rome', 'que', 'ut quem', 'ſides', 'Czfarez', 'epifcopoy']

claims.claim: At Bizya he also said: 'his, qui hec recipiunt, nunquam sum communicaturus.' Kept to the records

Condemnation and sentence: a synod anathematized 'sanctum Maximum, ejusque discipulum beatum Anastasium, necnon sanctissimum papam Martinum'; 'sententiam tulit præsens synodus'; the decree: 'Maximo ac utroque Anastasio, eorum flagris dorsa cædat ... linguam) ab imo intus abscindat ... dexteram ferro auferat ... urbis Augustæ regiones duodecim totas lustraverit, sempiterno exsilio ... Lazicem relegavit'
Theophanes on the mutilation: Constans 'illam sancti linguam una cum illius dextera abscidit' (Migne's Latin)

The two Anastasii: the disciple Anastasius, and 'Anastasium alterum' who 'Romanæ Ecclesiæ apocrisiarius audiebat' (Life). The envoy writes as 'Anastasius exiguus misericordia Dei presbyter et monachus' to Theodosius of Gangra. 'The envoy' renders 'apocrisiarius'. The sentence calls only one of them 'discipulum' (PG90 l.11469-11473). François Combefis's notes ('FR. COMBEFISII NOTAE AD VITAM S. MAXIMI'): the envoy and Maximus were 'quasi sodales exstiterint, non alter alterius discipulus'; 'nunquam tamen ipse Maximus discipulum vocat' the envoy, 'sed honorificentiori nomine, dominum meum'. The brief says 'two companions'

Exile among the Lazi, the envoy's letter: arrived 'ad amicorum Christi regionem Lazorum vi Idus Junias, v Indict.'; Maximus, unable to ride, carried on a litter: 'plectentes virgulas ex eis quasi lectulum texuissent, bajulantes detulerunt, et incluserunt in castro Schemari vocitato, juxta gentem illorum qui dicuntur Alani'
claims.witness: PG90 l.11685-11704 [OCR forms: 'v1 Idus', 'plecten- tes', 'Sche- mari']

claims.claim: Death foretold and date: 'Tertio decimo die Augusti mensis hujus instantis, quintæ dictæ indictionis, feria septima assumet me Dominus, quod et factum est. Igitur tertio decimo die prædicti Augusti mensis præteritæ v indictionis'. The Life: 'tertia decima scilicet mensis Augusti'. Migne's running head: 'ANNUS 662.'. The brief gives the day only, with the envoy attached ('the envoy adds'); the year is on the card
claims.witness: PG90 l.11672-11674, 11748-11752, 6574-6576, 138-141 [OCR forms: 'quintz dictz (b)', 'ſeria se- ptima', 'SACULUM VI.']

claims.claim: Age: Fabricius, 'in Lazicos deportatus obiit in carcere a. C. [year lost in OCR] ætatis 82'
claims.witness: PG90 l.277-279 [OCR forms: '@latis 82' read as 'ætatis 82'; the year after 'a. C.' is not legible]

claims.claim: The tomb: 'tres lampades luciferæ per singulas noctes sanctum sancti illius martyris monumentum illustrant' (the envoy's letter); the Life, 'lucidæ tres faces'

Lateran acts and Maximus: Severinus Binius, in Mansi 10, 'Quod in actis concilii nulla mentio reperiatur Maximi, mirum videri non debet', since abbots had 'non decidendi & subscribendi, sed tantum consulendi facultatem'. Among the Greek monks' signatures: 'Maximus monachus, similiter.', next to 'Anastasius monachus, similiter.'
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.117079-117081 (heading 'Notæ Severini Binii'), 117103-117112, 92670-92674 [OCR forms: long s as 'f', 'SEVERINi BiNil-', 'tantrum', 'Anattafius']

claims.claim: Theophanes on the exile: Constans had 'Sanctissimum Martinum et Maximum Cpolim adduci jussit, eosque tormentis excruciatos in exsilium deportari ad Chersonesi plagas'

Constantinople III (680-681), in Percival's English (NPNF 2.14): 'in him are two natural wills and two natural operations indivisibly ... And these two natural wills are not contrary the one to the other ... but his human will follows and that not as resisting and reluctant, but rather as subject to his divine and omnipotent will'. 'The Sixth Ecumenical Council met on November 7, 680'

At the same council, Macarius of Antioch's profession: 'eum qui nuper est exortus infaustum Maximum cum impiis ejus discipulis' among those he anathematizes; Macarius in NPNF: 'I do not say that there are two wills or two operations'. The council answered: 'To Macarius the heretic, anathema!' and 'with the best of cause we anathematize and depose Macarius, who was bishop of Antioch'
claims.witness: MANSI11 l.74364-74367; NPNF14 l.25675-25684 [OCR forms: 'infanftum', 'difcipulis']; NPNF14 l.25749, 25997

claims.claim: Fabricius: 'Theologus et confessor a Græcis appellatur, sanctisque una cum Anastasio, discipulo, ab Ecclesia ascribitur'; he says Maximus took part in the Lateran synod of 649 ('concilio Lateranensi a. 649, sub Martino I papa, interfuisset')
claims.witness: PG90 l.275-281 (notice from 'Bibliotheca Græca, ed. Harles', l.264-266) [OCR forms: 'conſessor', 'Crœca, ed. Hartes', 'a, 649']

claims.claim: Who wrote the Greek Life: Fabricius, 'legitur Vita ejus, scripta ab Anastasio, apocrisiario, discipulo'; 'Eamdem Vitam laudat Allatius ... ubi auctorem incertum prodit'. The Life itself cites '(Anastasius scilicet apocrisiarius) tradidit' for the other Anastasius's death. Its editor is 'Fr. Franciscus Combefis', Paris 1675

Three years in the fort: the Life, 'Divino autem Maximo [triennium] jam in Alaniæ castro incluso', the word in brackets in the Latin; the envoy's letter dates the arrival to 8 June and the death to 13 August of the fifth indiction

Key works: Capita de charitate, to 'pater Elpidi', 'pari quatuor Evangeliis numero, centenis comprehensum capitibus', gathered 'perlustratis atque excussis sanctorum Patrum libris ac scriptis'; Quæstiones ad Thalassium, 'MAXIMI HUMILIS MONACHI ... AD SANCTISSIMUM PRESBYTERUM AC PRÆPOSITUM THALASSIUM DE SCRIPTURÆ SACRÆ QUÆSTIONIBUS AC DUBIIS'; the Disputation with Pyrrhus (PG 91). The card says 'set in hundreds to match the four Gospels', not a hundred to each Gospel
claims.witness: PG90 l.76062-76085, 17168-17180; PG91 l.15040-15120 [OCR forms: 'ganctitati', 'san- ctorum', 'PRESBYTELR UM AC PREPOSITUX THALASSIUNM', 'QUEASTIONIBUS AG']

claims.claim: Card traditions: the census lists Maximus in the people of both 'The Byzantine Imperial Church (Heraclian & Iconoclast Eras)' (year 628) and 'Latin African Christianity under Byzantium' (year 632; dates 533-c. 698)
claims.witness: cic-website/data/world-census.json, movements byzantine-imperial-church-heraclian-iconoclast and latin-africa-under-byzantium, people lists

claims.claim: His own side's record: the Relatio calls him 'Dei servus' (l.6802 and throughout) and 'sanctus ... senex' (l.8276). The brief says 'his own side's record'
Fabricius's initials: 'J. A. Fabricius' is held, e.g. in the Antiphonary of Bangor volume; the card's first mention reads 'J. A. Fabricius'

contested_claims.claim: Whether Maximus took part in the Lateran synod of 649
sides: For: Fabricius, 'concilio Lateranensi a. 649, sub Martino I papa, interfuisset' (PG90 l.279-281); Theophanes, who has Maximus stir Martin to hold it (THEOPHANES l.60747-60752); a 'Maximus monachus' among the Greek monks' signatures, unidentified in the text (MANSI10 l.92672)
Against or unproved: Severinus Binius, 'in actis concilii nulla mentio reperiatur Maximi', abbots having only a right to advise (MANSI10 l.117103-117112)

contested_claims.claim: Who wrote the Greek Life (Vita ac Certamen)
sides: Anastasius the envoy, his disciple: Fabricius's notice (PG90 l.282-284)
Author uncertain: Leo Allatius, as Fabricius reports (PG90 l.285-286); the Life cites Anastasius the envoy as its source (PG90 l.6540-6542)

contested_claims.claim: How long Maximus lived in his last prison
sides: Three years: the Life's Latin, '[triennium]' in brackets (PG90 l.6570-6571)
One summer: the envoy's letter, arrival 'vi Idus Junias, v Indict.' and death on 13 August of the same fifth indiction (PG90 l.11685-11688, 11748-11752)

contested_claims.claim: Where Maximus was last exiled
sides: Among the Lazi, at Schemaris near the Alans: the sentence and the envoy's letter (PG90 l.11537-11538, 11695-11704)
The region of Cherson, with Martin: Theophanes (THEOPHANES l.60845-60849)

absent_details.detail: His birth year
absent_details.note: No held source gives one. Fabricius gives his age at death as eighty-two, but the year in that line is not legible in the OCR (PG90 l.279). The Library header's 'c. 580' is not used.

absent_details.detail: A held English translation of his works or of the record of his trials
absent_details.note: None found. The PG 90 and PG 91 files are Greek with Latin; the Greek OCR is unreadable, so every reading here is from the Latin. Mansi 11 reprints the Latin of the trials (l.740-8350).

absent_details.detail: Who set down the Record of the hearing
absent_details.note: The held text gives the title and Anastasius the Librarian's Latin (PG90 l.289-293, 6728-6747) but no author line was found. The census's 'written by a disciple who was present' is not used.

claims.claim: The seizure, Martin's second letter to Theodore (Mansi 10, 'XV. AD THEODORUM'): 'ante altare ecclesiæ lectulum meum habebam in quo jacebam'; the soldiers 'tenentes lanceas & spathas suas, quin & arcus suos paratos una cum scutis suis'; 'Quemadmodum namque in hiemali tempore vento valide flante folia ex arboribus concussa cadunt, ita percutiebantur armis candelæ sanctæ ecclesiæ'. He had been ill 'ab Octobrio mense usque ad prædictum tempus'. Told in modern words
claims.witness: MANSI10 (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-10-lat_welter-facsimile1901.txt) l.87304-87306, 87327-87339, 87399-87401 [OCR forms: long s as 'f', 'alrare ecclefiz', 'fpathas', '{cu- tis', 'fanée', 'infrmus', 'Ofobrio']

claims.claim: The church is the Lateran: 'privatim mansi in ecclesia salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi, quæ cognominatur Constantiniana ... & est juxta episcopium'; the Book of the Popes holds the synod 'secundum ecclesiam salvatoris juxta episcopium Lateranense'

He gave himself up rather than see blood shed: 'melius judicavi decies mori, quam unius cujuscumque sanguinem in terram fundi'; 'Eadem itaque hora dedi meipsum ad exhibendum imperatori, & non resistendum.' Told in modern words

Theodore: the letters open 'Martinus Theodoro sincera affectione dilecto fratri' (XIV) and 'Martinus Theodoro' (XV). 'A dear friend' renders 'dilecto fratri'. Louis Duchesne: the second letter 'fut écrite quelque temps après son arrivée à Constantinople, en octobre ou en novembre 654'
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.87158-87162, 87304-87310; DUCHESNE LP1 (liber-pontificalis_texte-introduction-commentaire-t1-lat-fra_duchesne1886.txt) l.163411-163413 [OCR forms: 'dileéto', 'Gonstantinople']

claims.claim: June 653: the Roman Breviary's bracketed date, 'treacherously taken [on the 17th day of June, 653,]'; William Dudley Foulke, in his notes to Paul the Deacon, Calliopas 'who in June, 653, coming to Rome with the army from Ravenna, seized the Pope'. Martin's letter: taken from the palace in the night before Wednesday 'tertiodecimo Kalendas Julias'
claims.witness: BREVIARY (roman-breviary_bute1908.txt) l.89160-89163; FOULKE (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt) l.9966-9970; MANSI10 l.87469-87473

claims.claim: Origin and year: the Book of the Popes, 'Martinus, de civitate Tudertina, provinciæ Tusciæ'; the Breviary, 'born at Todi in Tuscany. At the beginning of his Popedom, [in the year 649,]'; Binius in Mansi 10: 'Anno Christi 649. die prima mensis Julii'

The Typos and Paul: Martin's speech, copied into the Book of the Popes (Duchesne: 'Tout ce long passage est emprunté mot à mot au discours du pape Martin'): Paul of Constantinople sought 'ut & clementissimo Principi suaderet typum exponere', a Typos 'nec unam, nec duas voluntates, aut operationes in Christo domino nostro definiens confiteri'; 'altare ... sanctæ nostræ sedis, quod erat in domo Placidiæ sacratum in venerabili oraculo, subvertens, diriperet', so that the envoys could not offer Mass there
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.81980-82010; DUCHESNE LP1 l.162717-162740 (Duchesne's text: 'Altare enim sanctae nostrae sedis, in domo Placidiae sacratum') [OCR forms: 'Conftantinopoliranz', 'fuaderet', 'Placidiz facratum']

claims.claim: The synod: 'congregavit episcopos in urbem Romam numero centum & quinque'; 'condemnaverunt Cyrum Alexandrinum, Sergium, Pyrrhum, & Paulum, patriarchas Constantinopolitanos'; copies sent 'per omnes tractus orientis & occidentis'. Duchesne: 'Les cinq sessions du concile de Latran eurent lieu les 5, 8, 17, 19 et 31 octobre 649.' The Breviary: 'a council of one-hundred-and-five Bishops'. The brief no longer tells the count in its own voice; 'for teaching one will' rests on Bede, 'principally against those who taught but one will and operation in Christ' (GILES l.10403-10405)

Olympius, the Book of the Popes: the emperor sent 'Olympium cubicularium & exarchum' with orders 'jubemus teneri Martinum'; God 'non illum permisit'; the sword-bearer struck blind at Mass, 'excæcavit spatharium Olympii exarchi'. The Roman Breviary's fifth lesson repeats the blinding: the lictor 'was struck with blindness' (BREV l.89131-89152). Kept to the card's What is uncertain. Olympius was sent 'ad regendam omnem Italiam' (l.82124-82126), so the brief and card call him governor of Italy; after his death 'Deinde directus est ab imperatore Theodorus exarchus, qui cognomento Calliopa dicitur' (l.82111-82113), so Calliopas is 'his successor'
Calliopas: 'directus est ab imperatore Theodorus exarchus, qui cognomento Calliopa dicitur ... Qui tollentes sanctissimum Martinum papam de ecclesia salvatoris ... perduxerunt Constantinopolim'

Naxos, Martin's letter: 'excepto dumtaxat in insula Naxia, quoniam ibi annum fecimus'; 'quadraginta & septem dies sunt hodie, ex quo non merui calida nec frigida aqua rigare me'. Duchesne: 'Le voyage de Rome à Constantinople dura un an et trois mois'
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.87518-87525; DUCHESNE LP1 l.162997-163001 [OCR forms: 'Borne']

claims.claim: The account sent west: 'Commemoratio eorum quæ ... acta sunt ... in sanctum ... Martinum papam ... per epistolam cujusdam Christianissimi, directam his qui sunt in occidente, seu Romæ, & in Africa, orthodoxis patribus'; Duchesne, 'expédié en Occident par un des clercs de sa suite'. The writer calls himself 'humilis & peccator famulus vester'
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.87561-87568, 87588; DUCHESNE LP1 l.162992-162995 [OCR forms: 'Chriftianifiimi', 'diredham', 'few Rome', 'orthodoxss']

claims.claim: Arrival and prison: 'septimo decimo die Septembrii mensis'; held 'nonaginta tres dies'; brought to the trial 'in portatoria sella: erat enim penitus æger'

The trial: Dorotheus swore 're vera unius consilii fuit cum Olympio'; Martin began 'Si vultis audire veritatem, dico vobis sequentia ... Quando factus est typus, & directus Romam ab imperatore', and was cut off by Troilus: 'Non inferas nobis hic de fide, de duello nunc scrutaris'. 'Præfectus Troilus' at l.87763. 'Rebellion' renders 'duello'. Told in modern words
claims.witness: MANSI10 l.87818-87826, 87732-87744, 87760-87765 [OCR forms: 'fadus eft ty- pus', 'interas', 'nune {cru- taris', 'prefedtus']

claims.claim: Stripped and chained: the treasurer told the prefect 'continuo membratim incide illum'; 'exuerunt exterius ejus pallium sacerdotalis stolæ'; 'circumposuerunt ferrea vincula in sanctam ejus cervicem'; led 'dehonestantes per medium civitatis'

Spared death: Binius, in Mansi 10, after Anastasius the Librarian, says he would have been martyred 'nisi Paulus Constantinopolitanus episcopus morti vicinus obstitisset'. The brief says only 'spared death'

To Cherson: 'Dictum est ergo, quia in Chersonam exulatur'; Martin, 'navigantes sancta quinta feria cenæ domini ... Idibus Maiis, & Chersonem pervenimus.' Duchesne: 'Martin fut embarqué à Hiéron, près Constantinople, le jeudi saint, 26 mars 655. Il arriva à Cherson (Sébastopol) le 15 mai suivant'. 'The next spring' (brief): the Commemoratio's counts, ninety-three days from 17 September and then 'octoginta quinque dies post primas nonaginta tres' (l.87653-87657, 87748, 88181-88182), with 'intolerabilis hiems' at the trial (l.87958)
Hunger at Cherson, letter XVI: 'ut panis in ea tantum nominetur, non tamen penitus videatur'

Forgotten, letter XVII: friends and kin 'sic funditus infelicitatis meæ obliti sunt, & nec scire volunt ... sive sim super terram, sive non sim'; and he wonders 'multo magis' at 'eos, qui sunt sanctissimi apostoli Petri ecclesiæ'. Duchesne: 'Il s'y plaint avec douceur d'être oublié de son église de Rome et prie Dieu pour elle et surtout pour son successeur'
His prayer: 'stabiliat corda eorum in orthodoxa fide ... & immobiles custodiat, præcipue pastorem qui eis nunc præesse monstratur'

Closing words: 'De humili namque hoc corpore meo & ipse dominus curam erit, ut sibi gubernare placet, sive in tribulationibus indefinentibus, sive in modico refrigerio. Dominus enim prope est, & quid sollicitus sum?' Told in modern words

claims.claim: Death and burial, the Commemoratio: 'recens revera confessor & martyr'; 'mense Septembrio, die sextadecima ... indictione quartadecima'; 'in tumulis sanctorum extra muros Chersonitarum civitatis quasi stadio uno', in the church of Mary 'quæ cognominatur Blachernes'

claims.claim: Burning of the canons, Michael: 'Avant de partir, il discuta avec le patriarche et les évêques au sujet de l'observation des canons ecclésiastiques : mais personne ne l'écouta ; tous lui conseillaient de s'accommoder au temps et aux événements. C'est pourquoi, il apporta le livre des canons ecclésiastiques et le fit brûler devant la porte du monastère du patriarche, en criant à haute voix : « Je brûle dans le feu, comme superflus et inutiles, les canons que vous foulez aux pieds et n'observez pas ».' (OCR 'ail temps', 'eccléslîxsûqvves et le fit brâlec devant la çovte du. ïaotvastère du p^ttviwYch^, [44(>] ei^ criant'); the patriarch is Julian: 'confia le siège au patriarche Mar Julianus'

Nemo autem aures ei praebuit ; sed omnes ut res tempori accommodaret hortabantur ; idcirco canonum ecclesiasticorum codicem attulit et ante valvas monasterii ubi patriarcha habitabat igne concremavit, alta voce proclamans : « canones a vobis conculcatos et minime custoditos quasi superfluos et inutiles comburo.»' (OCR 'e/ cura', 'Juliana', 'concre- ... raavit', 'concultatos')

Michael and Bar Hebraeus belong to Jacob's church: Michael 'PATRIARCHE JACORITE D'ANTIOCHE (II66-II99)' (title page, OCR); Bar Hebraeus's father passed from Judaism to Christianity 'in secta Jacobitica', the editors' conjecture, and Bar Hebraeus was born 1226

Life, Michael: 'A cette époque florissait Jacques le Rhéteur, surnommé d'Edesse, parce qu'il fut, par la suite, ordonné évêque pour Edesse, par les mains du patriarche Athanase, l'Interprète des Écritures, surnommé Baladaya.' 'Il était originaire de la région d'Antioche, du village appelé 'Ayndâbâ, dans le pays de Goumah. Dans sa jeunesse, il fut élevé près de Cyriacus, visiteur de ce lieu, homme pieux. Il lut tout l'Ancien et le Nouveau Testament et les Docteurs exactement. Ensuite, il alla au monastère d'Aphtonia et y prit l'habit monastique. Il y étudia soigneusement les Psaumes en langue grecque, la lecture des livres et la langue (grecque); de là, il se rendit à Alexandrie. Il y resta un certain temps et y amassa des connaissances; puis il s'en revint en Syrie, et arriva à Edesse.' (OCR 'surnomméd'Edesse', 'parce qu^il', 'Goumah^', 'monas-^ tère')

Bar Hebraeus on the same: 'ex Indaba castello regionis Gumiae in agro Antiocheno oriundus, in monasterio Aphtonii seu Kenserinensi graecam linguam et sacrorum librorum lectionem accurate didicit. Inde Alexandriam profectus ibique eruditus, in Syriam postliminio reversus est.' (OCR 'gracani', 'Alexan- driani')

claims.claim: Audience in the garden: 'ipsi soli, absque episcopis qui cum ipso erant, permisit Calipha accedere ad se equo insidentem et in horto ambulantem'. (The participles most naturally describe the caliph, on horseback in the garden; the brief says only that he let Dionysius come to him alone in his garden.)

Baghdad and the edict of ten men: 'Ob hanc igitur causam patriarcha descendit Bagdadum'; the edict 'ut si convenirent decem viri cujuscumque religionis ... et antistitem sibi constituere vellent, nemo eos impediret'; Lazarus, 'legaliter judicatus, condemnatus ac depositus auderet dicere : » nobis edictum datum est ut si decem e nobis convenerint licet nobis antistitem constituere.'

Dionysius's answer: 'a quo tempore patres nostri civitates multas vobis tradiderunt, inter nos et vos exstare promissiones et pacta, de non immutandis contra nos legibus nostris; manifestum vero est legem absque legislatore non posse servari; una porro ex legibus nostris est principatus noster ecclesiasticus' (OCR 'scitsapientia tua.aquo', 'promis- siones')
The jurists: Christians are not to be forced 'ad mutandam eorum fidei professionem eorumque consuetudines, modo servent subjectionem nobis debitam et tranquilli remaneant' (kept to the records)

Al-Ma'mun's ruling: 'quod a gradu et dignitate removeatis et deponatis peccatorem non prohibemus vobis ; quod autem ejiciatis eum ab ecclesia et ab oratione prohibeatis fas vobis non judicamus; peccatores quippe praesertim oportet orare et petere a Deo remissionem delicti.' Dionysius 'discessit a Mamone ... laudatus a legisperitis (?) propter animi fortitudinem'. Date: 'mense Adar (Martio) anni 1140 (Chr. 829)' (OCR 'proliibcmus', 'ejiciatis cum', 'Adar (3/arf«o)', '{C/ir. 829)')
Bar Hebraeus born 1226: 'Hanc lucem primum aspexit anno oerae Christianm 1226, in urbe Melitina' (OCR 'oerae Christianm')

Monk of Kenneshre: Theodore of the monastery of Mar Jacob of Kaisum: 'Venit, inquit, ad nos frater Dionysius monachus, e coenobio Mar Joannis Bar-aphtonii, quod est monasterium Kenserinense, et duobus annis apud nos commoratus est' (OCR 'A^cnit', 'ctcnolho', 'Joanuis Bar- aphtonii', 'esst', 'Ken- serinense')

His own account of being seized, in Bar Hebraeus's Latin: 'Ait hic ipse Dionysius'; 'Eram quippe hominum minimus et maxime contemptibilis'; the fathers 'praemiserunt duos monachos cordatos ad monasterium Mar Jacobi, ubi commorabar, quia incolae Kenserinenses dispersi erant. Ingressi igitur ad me apprehenderunt me et custodierunt tanquam malefactorem, donec venirent episcopi'; 'quum assererem infirmitatem meam ac insufficientiam cum fletu et prostrationibus, irruerunt violenter in me' (OCR 'fletuet', 'custo- dierunt')

Ordinations: 'die Veneris ordinarunt me diaconum in monasterio Estunse, et die sabbati presbyterum in coenobio Mar Zachaeae, et die dominica, prima Ab (Augusti) anni 1129 (Chr. 818) promoverunt me ad perfectum ordinem summi sacerdotii in ecclesia catholica urbis Callinici' (OCR 'Estunse*', 'Mar Zacli8e*', '{Augusti)', '(Chr. 818)'); 'Imposuit autem ei manum Theodosius Callinici'

First voyage to Egypt: 'Anno autem Graecorum 1136 (Chr. 823), quum Emirus Abdallah descendisset in Aegyptum, Mohammed, ejus frater, quaecumque invenit nova aedificia in ecclesiis Edessenis vastavit ... Quapropter accinxit se patriarcha in Aegyptum. Exorta est autem tempestas ... vix se recipere potuit ad portum urbis Tanis ... Occurrerunt ei christiani hujus urbis ad triginta prope millia. Venit etiam illuc ad eum Jacobus patriarcha, Alexandriae papa' (OCR '(CAr. 823)', 'jEgyptura', 'qumcumque', '.^i^ptum', 'Alexandri® papa')

Dionysius's words at Tanis: 'Ait autem Mar Dionysius: «tunc commemoravimus eis verba Athanasii patriarchae cognomento Camelarii ... et agnovimus debilitatas esse recitationes ex eo quod neglecta fuerit apud eos scientia Scripturarum.»' (kept to the records)

The emir: Abdallah, son of Tahir ('ad Abdallah, Tahiri filium'); in Egypt Dionysius 'ingressus est ad Tahirum. Quia porro Emiro gratissimus erat, reprehendit eum ... dicens : »quid cogebat te ut venires in Aegyptum, quum posses per epistolam significare mihi quid velles? »'; 'Tunc Emirus propria manu scripsit fratri suo eum reprehendens'; tax at Tanis: 'Quinque enim denarii exigebantur a quacumque persona sive divite sive paupere. Praecepit igitur Emirus ut a divitibus quadraginta et octo zuzae, a mediis viginti quatuor, a pauperibus vero duodecim, acciperentur.' (OCR '.lEgyptum', 'divito', 'zuz»')

Second journey, with al-Ma'mun: 'Eodem anno venit Calipha Mamon Chisumam ... Mandavit autem Calipha patriarcham secum proficisci in Aegyptum, ut eum legatum mitteret ad Christianos Byamitas, in regione inferiore Aegypti habitantes, ut a rebellione reverterentur. Quumque profectus esset patriarcha noster cum patriarcha Aegypti Josepho ad eos reconciliandos, Apschinus, militiae praefectus, pacem noluit, sed villas eorum, vineas hortosque igne comburens, plurimos quidem interfecit, reliquos vero vinctos navibus Antiochiam misit, et exinde Bagdadum. Multi autem in via mortui sunt. Patriarcha ad Mamonem reversus ei denuntiavit Byamitas opprimi' (OCR 'patriarchm', 'cum lega- tum', '/Egyptum', 'Ap- schinus', 'Byaniitas')
The editors on the rebels' names: 'Renaudotius eos [...]tas appellat ... Eosdem [...]anos vocat Lequien' (OCR 'Ilenaudotius eos Itschammiri* tas appellat'; 'Baammjfrilanos vocat Lequicn')

On the Coptic church: 'De papa Josepho et episcopis Aegypti patriarcha haec narrat : «eos esse invenimus populum pudicum, sincerum ... et tanto honore excepti fuimus ut omnem praerogativam papae in ditione sua debitam nobis tribuerent ... Sublatum enim eis erat studium Scripturarum sanctarum ... siquidem absque ducentis aut trecentis daricis non potest quis pervenire ad summum pontificatum' (OCR 'prscrogativam', 'pontitica- tura')

The pyramids: 'Addit rursus patriarcha : « vidimus in Aegypto istas pyramides ... nec horrea sunt Josephi, ut quidam opinati sunt, sed admiranda aedificia, super sepulchra antiquorum regum exstructa, obliqua et solida, non cava et vacua' (OCR '/Egypto', 'ttsiiiicia')

Ordained Thomas at Tagrit: 'primatu post patriarcham Antiochenum Maphriano remanente in toto Oriente. Quia porro Daniel Tagriti obierat, elegit et ordinavit Tagriti Thomam'; vol. 3: Thomas 'Ordinatus fuit a Dionysio Telmaharensi patriarcha'

History written for John of Dara and its closing letter: 'calamitates omnis generis multiplicatae sunt ab Arabibus in Christianos ubique locorum per exactiones intolerandas, de quibus sic scribit Dionysius ad Joannem Darae, cujus rogatu exaravit Chronicon suum : « necesse non habeo gravare intelligentiam tuam quantis in calamitatibus verser ita ut noctes absque somno, dies absque ulla quiete transeam ... Fleo igitur et lugeo vitam meam, quod infelix ego propter peccata mea relictus sim ad bibendum calicem istum, utque patiar et dolore prematur cor meum quando oculis meis video clades poenasque quas sufferunt filii Ecclesiae ... Unica igitur mihi superest a malis liberatio, mors scilicet, quam tanquam rem bonam faustamque appeto. » Hic absolvit beatus ille vir Chronicon suum.' (OCR 'Fico igitur', 'pocnasque', 'Ecclesim', 'Joannem Da- ra:*')

Death and burial: 'Obiit autem vigesima secunda mensis Ab (Augusti) anni millesimi centesimi quinquagesimi sexti (Chr. 845) et sepultus est in monasterio Kenserinensi ... ordinavit centum episcopos' (OCR '(Auffusti)', '(<7>4r. 845)'). The count of years in office reads 'annis septem* decim' in the OCR and is not used

Preface, in Michael: 'Comme à partir d'ici commence le patriarche Denys, surnommé de Tell Mahrê, voici que je place d'abord la Préface de ses écrits'; 'ô mon fils spirituel, Iwannis, métropolitain de Dara'; 'tu n'as pas considéré la vieillesse qui couvre ma tête ... mais que je passe de village en village, et me transporte d'un lieu à un autre (subissant) de longs et pénibles voyages, des stations et des prostrations à la porte des princes avec le mépris et l'humiliation qui y sont inhérents' (OCR 'patriaj^che', 'con- sidéré', 'autre^')

Theophilus of Edessa and Qura of Batna: 'L'un d'eux, Theophilus d'Edesse, qui était chalcédonien et regardait comme son héritage la haine des Orthodoxes, laissa frauduleusement de côté toutes les histoires dans lesquelles on faisait mémoire de l'un des nôtres. C'est pourquoi nous continuerons la série des premiers, et nous commencerons là où s'arrête Qourâ de Batna'
Michael's range for him: 'Denys le patriarche écrivit depuis Maurice jusqu'à Théophile, l'empereur des Grecs, et Haroun, l'émir des Arabes.'
Michael's own times: title page 'PATRIARCHE JACORITE D'ANTIOCHE (II66-II99)' (OCR 'JACORITE', 'II66-II99')

The grandfather: 'Le patriarche Denys de Tell Mahré, qui rapporte ces choses, ajoute : « J'ai pris ces choses des histoires de Daniel, fils de Samuel, du Tour 'Abdîn, mon grand-père maternel. Pour moi, je crois que l'image était chez les Chalcédoniens d'Édesse ...' (census person-list quote verified at l.36788-36790)

Michael copies from him: 'Note marginale : Cette lettre du patriarche Petrus est écrite tout au long dans le livre de Denys de Tell Mahrê. Nous en avons placé ici des extraits' (OCR 'lis>re'); Peter is 'Petrus, patriarche d'Antioche' (l.28029)
Chabot: 'Tout ce qui suit jusqu'à la fin de ce chap. est tiré de Denys de Tell Mahrê. C'est le seul chapitre de sa Chronique dont nous ayons le texte.'
The heading at the start of Michael's chronicle names 'Denys de Tell-Mahré' among its sources; Chabot: 'J'ai acquis la conviction que ce titre est apocryphe.'

Church that refused Chalcedon (context for 'Syriac Orthodox'): Isaiah of Edessa to Heraclius, 'Si tu n'anathématises pas par écrit le synode de Chalcédoine et le Tome de Léon, je ne te laisserai pas toucher les mystères.'

Eutychius of Alexandria on the same revolt: 'Post haec tumultuati sunt Al Bimaidae ... in inferiore terrae Aegyptiacae parte ... Hi igitur rebelles facti vectigal et tributum pendere noluerunt. Quod cum Al Mamuni nuntiatum esset, misit ille Almotasemum copiis instructum in Aegyptum ... feminasque ipsorum et liberos Bagdadum captivos abduxit ... Tum et ipse Al Mamun comitante Al Motasemo in Aegyptum profectus est' (OCR 'Al Bimaid#', 'Xgypliacæ', 'ſacti', 'ſeminasque'). No patriarch is named. Bar Hebraeus's editors' 'totidem verbis' (BH1 l.21826-21828) overstates the match

Renaudot, reporting Makrizi: 'rebellasse Coptitas, & anno Hegirae 216 Afschinum adversus eos copias duxisse, neque subactos, antequam Almamon in Aegyptum advenisset; qui causa cognita multos supplicio capitis condemnavit, foeminas & pueros vendi jussit' (OCR long s); and on the first voyage: 'Dionysius Patriarcha Jacobitarum Antiochenus, qui dudum fama Jacobi excitatus eum videre optabat, advenit, & dies multos apud illum cum mutua utriusque consolatione transegit' (OCR 'Jacobi- tamm', 'cum vi- opubat')

Nomocanon: 'uti definiunt Dionysius patriarcha Telmaharensis, et religiosus Iacobus Edessae', on kinship through the sponsors at a wedding ('in sponsione coronarum'); title 'ECCLESIAE ANTIOCHENAE SYRORUM NOMOCANON A GREGORIO ABULPHARAGIO BAR-HEBRAEO' (OCR 'patriarcha. Telmaharensis , et. religiosus')

Where Tel Mahre was: W. Wright's footnote on 'Dionysius of Tell-Mahré*': '... in Arabic [Arabic], a small town on the river Balikh, between ar-Rakkah and Hisn Maslamah, according to Yáküt in the Mujam al-Buldan' (OCR 'A ISS', 'Yáküàt')

contested_claims.claim: Whether the shorter chronicle ending about 775 is Dionysius's
sides: For Dionysius: Joseph Assemani, who took it for Dionysius's shorter chronicle ('Assemanus summarium Chronici brevioris Dionysii ... usque ad annum Graecorum 1086, Christi 775, describit', BH1 (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872.txt) l.20440-20443); Bar Hebraeus's editors, who follow him: 'idque de prolixiori ejusdem Chronico intelligendum; nam Chronicon brevius, quod in Scetensi coenobio Assemanus nactus est, anno circiter 775 terminatur, idemque non Joanni Darensi, sed Georgio Amidae chorepiscopo ... nuncupatum est. Ita Assemanus' (BH1 (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872.txt) l.22351-22366); W. Wright, who calls the Vatican chronicle Dionysius's 'own larger work' (WRIGHT (joshua-the-stylite_chronicle_wright1882.txt) l.292-298); Chabot in 1895, 'Quatrième partie de la Chronique de Denys de Tell-Mahré' (MICHAEL1 (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome1-livres-i-vii-fra_chabot1899.txt) l.62784-62784)

Against: J.-B. Chabot by 1899, 'Pseudo-Denys' (MICHAEL1 (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome1-livres-i-vii-fra_chabot1899.txt) l.13650-13650; MICHAEL1 (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome1-livres-i-vii-fra_chabot1899.txt) l.59560-59560; MICHAEL2 (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901.txt) l.36430-36430); J. K. Fotheringham, 'chronica anonymi cuiusdam monachi olim per errorem Dionysio Telmaharensi tributa' (FOTHERINGHAM (jerome_eusebii-chronici-canones-lat_fotheringham1923.txt) l.189-191), title page 1923 (FOTHERINGHAM (jerome_eusebii-chronici-canones-lat_fotheringham1923.txt) l.54-54)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the al-Ma'mun hearing is Dionysius's own account
sides: Bar Hebraeus tells it in narrative, without 'Ait Dionysius' (BH1 (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872.txt) l.21478-21716)

Issaverdens: 'One of the greatest glories of the Armenian Church in this century was Gregor of Nareg'

Boré: 'Au milieu de la nuit du dixième siècle le génie de S. Grégoire de Nareg jette la plus vive lumière'; 'le placent, aux yeux des Arméniens, parmi les lyriques les plus estimés des autres peuples. Ses élégies sacrées ont une onction touchante' (OCR 'liuit','géoie')

Commentary on the Song of Songs, in Parisot's Latin: 'Ea praecipue apud nos quae de lingua graeca vel syriaca interpretata fuerunt, obscure versa sunt in linguam armeniacam' (Gregorius Narekensis, Explicatio Cantici Canticorum, Venetiis, 1789, pp. 27-28)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Gregory sought union with the Greeks through Chalcedon
sides: Yes, he tried to persuade the Armenians to accept Chalcedon and was summoned to Ani for it: Michael Chamich (CHAMICH l.4817-4840) and James Issaverdens (ISSAV l.5273-5288), both Mekhitarists of Venice, whose order Malachia Ormanian names in the movement that formed the Armeno-Catholics (ORMANIAN l.9124-9135)
He worked to calm the quarrels over the orthodoxy of the fathers of Chalcedon, then withdrew to Narek: Giovanni de Serpos (SERPOS2 l.1695-1712)
Suspected of leaning toward reconciliation with the Greeks and persecuted in 977: Charles Lebeau, as Frédéric Macler reports him (MACLER l.7770-7774)
Malachia Ormanian's held book names him only for the Narek and the saints' list (ORMANIAN l.7744-7748, 8582-8583)

contested_claims.claim: His age when he wrote the Song of Songs commentary
sides: Twenty-six: Chamich (CHAMICH l.4888-4891); Issaverdens (ISSAV l.5331-5340)
Twenty, for a Bagratid king: Serpos (SERPOS2 l.1688-1693)

absent_details.detail: The text of the Narek
absent_details.note: The book itself is not held. Only the opening lines of discourses xii and xli (CONYBEARE l.34475-34477, 34530-34531) and two lines of the first panegyric on Jacob of Nisibis, in Parisot's Latin from the 1726 Book of Prayers (PARISOT l.1663-1672, 1720-1721), are held. The two liturgy prayers are given whole in Issaverdens's English (ISSRIT l.848-915), with no claim there that they come from the Narek.

absent_details.detail: A held witness from Gregory's own lifetime
absent_details.note: Stepanos of Taron, who knew some of these teachers in his youth and wrote soon after 1004 (his third book runs 'de l'an 887 à l'an 1005', MACLER l.438-442; 'Dans notre jeunesse', l.4346-4347), describes Narek and its monk Anania but does not name Gregory in either held translation (GELZER, MACLER; grep for Narek, Grigor, Grégoire, Gregor). The held life rests on Chamich (1784), Serpos (1786), Issaverdens (1875) and Ormanian (1912).
